newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Foreigners bought $2 bln Russia T-bills Aug-Oct.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners bought $2 bln Russia T-bills Aug-Oct.

text.p: Foreign investment in Russian GKO discount Treasury bills exceeded $2.05-2.15 billion between August 15, when a new investment regime got under way, and October 15, a top central bank official said.

"October was the best month, when non-residents exceeded half a monthly plan within a week, on news about Russia's credit rating and the central bank's decision to cut the yield to 16 percent," deputy chairman Andrei Kozlov told Reuters.
The central bank decided to cut the dollar yield on forward deals with T-bills for non-resident investors to 16 percent from 19 percent from October 16.
From August 15 non-residents have been able open rouble accounts at Russian banks chosen by the central bank and use the funds to buy T-bills and interest-bearing OFZ government bonds.
Kozlov said Russia limited total foreign October investment at $1 billion. Net investment amounted to $850-$900 million by October 15.
In August foreigners invested $350-$400 million compared to a limit of $700 million and in September $850 million compared to a limit of $1 billion.
Kozlov said the central bank plans to cut the forward term not earlier than from January 1, 1997 and not more than up to two months.
Currently the minimum forward deal term is three months.
